accepted.sentence: Players change pitch by tightening or relaxing their buzzing lips, selecting different notes within the instrument’s harmonic series.
Brief tongue contact interrupts the airstream at note beginnings, producing clear attacks without stopping the breath completely.
Combining valve presses with different lip-selected harmonics provides a chromatic range across several registers.
Steady abdominal airflow helps maintain a centered tone through long phrases and dynamic changes.
To play higher notes, performers increase lip tension and direct faster air through the mouthpiece.
A mute placed inside the bell alters the tone color and may reduce projection, depending on its design.
For a slur, performers keep airflow continuous while changing lip vibration between notes, avoiding a fresh tongue attack.
In the common B-flat version, written C sounds as concert B-flat, so orchestral parts are transposed for performers.
